reader.notes: A file with no RECORD clause and record descriptions of 10 and 20 characters is fixed at 20 (D-FRA), so WRITE R1 writes 20 characters and a REWRITE R1 of that record answers 44. That is GR10 applied to a 20-character record. 1985 leaves the record type implementor-defined (VII.3.8.4 GR13 makes even format 3 either fixed or variable, beside the same 'completely defined in the record description entry' wording as GR1), so I read it as latitude, not a defect. A refuter may want to weigh it.

refuter.evidence: The reader's open question (a file with no RECORD clause and records of 10 and 20 is fixed at 20, so REWRITE of the 10-character record is 44) is settled by explicit 1985 text: §1985:II.2.1.4.3 'it is implementor defined whether fixed length or variable length records are obtained' where no RECORD clause is specified or it specifies a range; the choice is documented (docs/conformance/7/DOC-A.1-147.md cites §1985:II.2.1.4.3), and under a fixed file II.2.1.4.1 lets every operation process only the one record size, so 44 is GR10 applied. Probes (refute-1985-025/src/rw10b.cob, rw10odo.cob, --std 85): RECORD VARYING DEPENDING ON: REWRITE FROM a 30- and a 3-character identifier with DLEN=8 over an 8-character record -> 00 and the file holds the 8 moved characters (size by data-name-1, VII.3.8.4 GR10a); DLEN=25 (over the maximum) -> 44, record unchanged; VARYING 10 TO 20 without DEPENDING: REWRITE of the 20-character description over a 10-character record -> 44, 10 over 10 -> 00, 10 over 20 -> 44 with the record area unaffected; format 3 RECORD CONTAINS 10 TO 20 gives variable records (II.2.1.4.3 latitude), 10 over 10 and 20 over 20 -> 00; ODO record with no RECORD clause (fixed at the 12-character maximum, VII.3.8.4 GR15): REWRITE at N=3 and N=4 over a 12-character record -> 00, consistent with the fixed choice. cite.py: OK §1985:VII.4.5.4 GR10; OK §1985:II.2.1.4.3 (2.1.4.3 Implementor-Defined Record Types); OK §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR1.
